text:
maria: quick brain dump — thinking we should move internal service-to-service APIs proto-first (gRPC) and put a tiny REST translation layer at the edge for external clients. main goals: typed contracts, cheaper runtime for internal calls, easier versioning. tradeoffs on quotas/routing?
aj: +1 on proto-first for internal. gRPC keeps payloads small and enables bidi streaming for some workloads. main worry: debugging/observability when we have translation layers.
sam: how do you imagine routing policies? tenant aware? model routing weight?
maria: yes tenant-aware routing. prefer routing decisions in control plane (console) so we can change weights without deploys. eg route by header X-Tenant or model-route header, fallback to default pool.
anya: for quotas I think we need per-tenant + per-route limits. e.g., tenant X has 100 rps per model-route, global soft cap for burst. enforcement at edge gateway + enforcement double-checked at runtime to avoid evasion.
kevin: double-enforcement means more complexity and a chance for mismatch. can we instead push soft throttle at edge and credit-based enforcement in runtime?
aj: credit-based sounds good. runtime can return `quota_status` header so gateway knows exact remaining tokens. avoids split-brain between components.
lisa: Telemetry: console wants per-route latency + token-cost breakdown and error-rate, not just p50/p99. We also need sample payloads for evals. How to propagate trace ids across translation layer?
maria: keep `x-request-id` and `x-trace` untouched in translation. translation layer must be transparent about headers. also include `x-proto-version` so we can map logs back to schema.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary of `edge-rest-shim:v2` started on cluster=us-west1 (10%).
sam: on canary: please ensure the shim adds `x-proto-version` and `x-original-path` for easier mapping. also log the selected internal method for each request.
anya: quota key composition: tenant + route + window-size (1s/1m) + billing-plan. We should document keys in console so SREs can correlate spikes.
aj: about gateway patterns — fully-transcoding gateway vs smart adapter. transcoding gateway just maps JSON <-> proto. smart adapter can do fallbacks, retries, merge requests. which do we want?
kevin: my vote is lightweight transcoding for edge (simplicity + perf), keep smart logic in internal services or an adapter tier behind the gateway. avoids fat gateway anti-pattern.
maria: agreed. avoid stuffing business fallback logic in the edge. policy routing decisions (weights, canary %) live in control plane and gateway reads them via cache.
lisa: console UX: routing policy editor should show effective path, percentage weights, affected tenants, and dry-run preview. plus a toggle for 'enforce quotas' vs 'simulate'.
aj: also visibility: when a tenant is routed to a new model variant we should surface request samples (redacted) and a diff of token-costs and latency. automatic alert if cost increases >10% or latency >20%.
sam: test plan for migration: 1) enable proto-first internally, 2) deploy shim in front of a subset of clients, 3) canary route some tenants to new path, 4) monitor metrics + abort on regressions. keep rollbacks cheap.
anya: edge auth — make sure the shim validates JWTs and attaches `x-tenant` claim as header for internal routing. Avoid trusting client-supplied headers.
kevin: proto schemas: we need stable field numbers and a deprecation policy. console should show compatible/non-compatible changes when someone tries to push a new proto.
maria: ops followups: - write a tiny envoy filter snippet for header mapping, - spec for quota key shapes, - console mockup for routing editor, - proto compatibility checker job. volunteers?
aj: I can take envoy filter snippet and quota key spec.
sam: I'll prototype the console mockup.
lisa: I'll own telemetry dashboard requirements and alert config.
anya: I'll draft the proto compatibility policy and registry hooks.
ops-bot: reminder: weekly infra sync Wednesday 10:30 — put this on agenda for 10m.
maria: thanks all. next: aj and sam to post PRs with early artifacts, we'll review in sync. :thumbsup:
